newsitem.title: FRANCE: France should probe seized Jewish assets - Klarsfeld.
newsitem.headline: France should probe seized Jewish assets - Klarsfeld.

text.p: A French probe into the seizure of apartments from Jews sent to Nazi death camps in World War Two should include the taking of their money, jewels and other assets, Nazi-hunter Serge Klarsfeld said on Wednesday .

The Paris city council halted a sale of apartments on Monday following allegations that some of the city-owned dwellings, mainly in the mediaeval Marais area where many Jews live, may have been seized from Jews during the war.

Klarsfeld, who had raised the issue of the property last year, told the Anglo-American Press Association in Paris that Jewish-owned buildings in other French cities, including Bordeaux in the southwest, were also involved.

"The money the Jews had on them when they arrived at the Drancy transit camp (outside Paris), as well as jewels and other valuables, were taken by the police chief and given to (state-run institutions). The money was sent to the Finance Ministry and was spent by the Treasury after the war," he said.

"The Jews were never reimbursed...The same applies to bank accounts, shares, other assets. Research must be done. It will show that part of the Jewish assets went into the public and private hands of people who are not Jews," he added.
In Italy and Belgium, Jewish assets which could not be traced to an heir were given to associations representing the Jewish community.
Klarsfeld said that only an official of the French administration could conduct a proper investigation.

"President Jacques Chirac said last year that France owed an eternal debt (for its part in the Final Solution). That debt could be paid by research, and by the value of the assets being given to Jewish associations," he said.
The French Jewish community urged the Paris city council on Sunday to report "on possible despoilment of Paris Jewish families under the collaborationist Vichy regime, and on compensation to them".

Their concern was stirred by a book, "Private Estate" by journalist Brigitte Vital-Durand, which said the Paris city council owns 150 buildings in the Marais, some of which had belonged to Jews, and that some property was sold without its history being disclosed.

The book said the population of part of the Marais had slumped to 5,000 from 25,000 during the war as Jewish families were deported or fled persecution. In total, about 75,000 Jews were deported from France to Hitler's death camps.

Holocaust survivors and their relatives have become more vocal in recent years in seeking to trace billions of dollars in assets seized by the Nazis, notably gold alleged to have been sent to Swiss banks during the war.
